rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Asked about owning two enslaved sisters, Ali says one verse permits them and another forbids them, so he neither commands nor forbids and will not do so himself or with his family.
rows.anchor: قال في الأختين المملوكتين أحلتهما آية وحرمتهما آية ولا آمر ولا أنهي ولا أحل ولا أحرم

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: When asked what he would do about the practice, Ali says that if authority were his, he would punish anyone who did it as a deterrent.
rows.anchor: عن قبيصة بن ذؤيب أن رجلا سأله عليه السلام عن ذلك فقال لو كان إلي من الأمر شيء

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A man who has married one enslaved sister must first remove her from his ownership by gifting or selling her before marrying the other; gifting her to his child suffices.
rows.anchor: إذا كانت عند الإنسان الأختان المملوكتان فنكح إحداهما ثم بدا له في الثانية فليس ينبغي له أن ينكح الأخرى

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: He explains the exception for owned women as a master ordering his slave to abstain from his enslaved wife, then having intercourse with her himself before returning her to the slave without a new marriage.
rows.anchor: هو أن يأمر الرجل عبده وتحته أمته فيقول له اعتزل امرأتك ولا تقربها ثم يحبسها عنه حتى تحيض

rows.speaker: أحدهما
rows.claim: If a man married his enslaved woman to his own slave, he may reclaim her at will; if she married another's slave, he must sell her first, after which the buyer may end or continue the marriage.
rows.anchor: عن أحدهما عليهما السلام في قول الله { والمحصنات من النساء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: When Fairoz al-Daylami became Muslim while married to two sisters, the Prophet told him to divorce whichever one he chose.
rows.anchor: عن فيروز الديلمي أنه أدركه الإسلام وتحته أختان فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم طلق أيتهما شئت

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali tells a man with two enslaved sisters, who had children by one and wanted the other, to free the first before having intercourse with the second.
rows.anchor: إن لي أختين مما ملكت يميني اتخذت إحداهما سرية وولدت لي أولادا ثم رغبت في الأخرى

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali says the scriptural kinship prohibitions for free women also apply to owned women, while the numerical limit differs; foster relations carry the same prohibitions as lineage.
rows.anchor: يحرم عليك مما ملكت يمينك ما يحرم عليك في كتاب الله من الحرائر إلا العدد أو قال إلا الأربع

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report in Bukhari and Muslim says the Prophet forbade combining a woman in marriage with her paternal aunt or maternal aunt.
rows.anchor: لا يجمع بين المرأة وعمتها ولا بين المرأة وخالتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai says Sunni reports support that prohibition, but reports from the Ahl al-Bayt Imams say otherwise, and the Qur'an supports their position.
rows.anchor: لكن المروي من طرق أئمة أهل البيت خلاف ذلك والكتاب يساعده

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: At Hunayn, companions hesitated to have intercourse with captured women because their polytheist husbands remained alive; the report says 4:24 then permitted them as war captives.
rows.anchor: بعث يوم حنين جيشا إلى أوطاس فلقوا عدوا فقاتلوهم فظهروا عليهم وأصابوا لهم سبايا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai notes that the same reported occasion involving captured women was also transmitted from Ibn Abbas through al-Tabarani.
rows.anchor: وروي ذلك عن الطبراني عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima relates that the verse concerned Mu'adhah, who left her elderly husband Shuja' with a cousin; Shuja' complained to the Prophet, who ordered her returned unless the cousin had consummated the relationship.
rows.anchor: نزلت في امرأة يقال لها معاذة وكانت تحت شيخ من بني سدوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai treats reported occasions attached especially to portions of verses as narrators' applications of the text, not genuine causes of revelation.
rows.anchor: أمثال هذه الأسباب المروية للنزول وخاصة فيما كانت متعلقة بأبعاض الآيات وأجزائها تطبيقات من الرواة وليست بأسباب حقيقية

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: In the report from al-Sadiq, al-muhsanat in 4:24 means women who already have husbands.
rows.anchor: قال هن ذوات الأزواج فقيل والمحصنات من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم قال هن العفائف

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: The same report interprets al-muhsanat among the People of the Book in 5:5 as chaste women.
rows.anchor: فقيل والمحصنات من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم قال هن العفائف

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: The Mujma' reports from al-Baqir that inability to afford marriage means lacking financial means.
rows.anchor: أي من لم يجد منكم غنى قال وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq says a free man should not marry an enslaved woman today, since the former financial barrier no longer applies when a free woman's dowry is no more than a slave woman's.
rows.anchor: والطول المهر ومهر الحرة اليوم مهر الأمة أو أقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai says wealth is one instance of the broader meaning of tawl, and the report establishes only disapproval, not prohibition.
rows.anchor: الغنى أحد مصاديق الطول كما تقدم والرواية لا تدل على أزيد من الكراهة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq rules that marrying an enslaved woman without her owners' permission is fornication, citing the command to marry them with their owners' consent.
rows.anchor: قال هو زنا إن الله تعالى يقول فانكحوهن بإذن أهلهن

rows.speaker: الرضا
rows.claim: Al-Rida permits temporary marriage with an enslaved woman when her owners consent, citing the same verse.
rows.anchor: قال نعم إن الله عز وجل يقول { فانكحوهن بإذن أهلهن }

rows.speaker: أحدهما
rows.claim: Asked what protection means in the phrase 'if they are protected,' one of the two Imams says it means consummating marriage; even without consummation, the woman is still liable to the prescribed penalty.
rows.anchor: قال يدخل بهن قلت فإن لم يدخل بهن ما عليهن حد؟ قال بلى

rows.speaker: حريز
rows.claim: Huraiz reports an answer defining a muhsan as someone who has enough to live on.
rows.anchor: عن حريز قال سألته عن المحصن فقال الذي عنده ما يغنيه

rows.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
rows.claim: Ali decrees fifty lashes for an enslaved man or woman who commits adultery, Muslim or non-Muslim, with neither stoning nor banishment.
rows.anchor: قضى أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام في العبيد والإماء إذا زنا أحدهم أن يجلد خمسين جلدة إن كان مسلما أو كافرا أو نصرانيا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: An enslaved man who falsely accuses a free person receives the full eighty lashes as a human right; adultery and wine-drinking are God's rights and incur half the penalty.
rows.anchor: عن عبد مملوك قذف حرا قال يجلد ثمانين هذا من حقوق الناس فأما ما كان من حقوق الله عز وجل فإنه يضرب نصف الحد

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Al-Baqir says an enslaved woman who commits adultery receives half the prescribed penalty whether married or unmarried.
rows.anchor: في الأمة تزني قال تجلد نصف الحد كان لها زوج أو لم يكن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas defines women who openly fornicate and women with secret lovers, explaining that pre-Islamic people condemned public but accepted hidden adultery; 6:151 forbids both.
rows.anchor: قال المسافحات المعلنات بالزنا المتخذات أخدان ذات الخليل الواحد قال كان أهل الجاهلية يحرمون ما ظهر من الزنا ويستحلون ما خفي

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Al-Baqir identifies the verse 'what you enjoy from them, give them their due' as the Qur'anic basis for temporary marriage.
rows.anchor: فقال نزلت في القرآن { فما استمتعتم به منهن فآتوهن أجورهن فريضة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: An unnamed transmitter reports al-Sadiq's wording of the verse with the addition 'for a specified term.'
rows.anchor: إلى أجل مسمى فآتوهن أجورهن فريضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai says reports from al-Baqir, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and Ibn Abbas transmit a 'specified term' reading; he takes such reports as indicating the intended meaning, not literal wording revealed.
rows.anchor: ولعل المراد بأمثال هذه الروايات الدلالة على المعنى المراد من الآية دون النزول اللفظي

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Al-Baqir says temporary marriage is permitted by God's Book and the Prophet until the Day of Resurrection, despite Umar's prohibition; he follows the Prophet's ruling.
rows.anchor: أحلها الله في كتابه وعلى لسان نبيه فهي حلال إلى يوم القيامة فقال يا أبا جعفر مثلك يقول هذا وقد حرمها عمر

rows.speaker: زرارة
rows.claim: Zarara narrates a dispute in which Ibn Umayr challenges al-Baqir for opposing Umar; al-Baqir offers mutual imprecation over whether the Prophet's ruling or Umar's claim is true.
rows.anchor: وأنا على قول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم، فهلم ألاعنك أن القول ما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: When Ibn Umayr invokes whether his own female relatives would accept temporary marriage, al-Baqir turns away after he mentions his family.
rows.anchor: فأعرض عنه أبو جعفر عليه السلام حين ذكر نساءه وبنات عمه

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq says temporary marriage was revealed in the Qur'an and practiced as a Sunna of the Messenger.
rows.anchor: قال المتعة نزل بها القرآن وجرت بها السنة من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Asked by Abu Hanifa whether women's temporary marriage is valid, al-Sadiq points him to 4:24; Abu Hanifa admits it seems he had never read the verse.
rows.anchor: فقال والله كأنها آية لم أقراها قط

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jaber reports that the Prophet allowed temporary marriage during campaigns and did not prohibit it.
rows.anchor: إنهم غزوا معه فأحل لهم المتعة ولم يحرمها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas recites the verse with a specified-term phrase in support of temporary marriage.
rows.anchor: إلى أجل مسمى فآتوهن أجورهن فريضة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Al-Baqir says a couple may mutually extend the term and payment after the agreed period; she remains unavailable to another man until a waiting period of two menstrual cycles ends.
rows.anchor: لا بأس بأن تزيدها وتزيدك إذا انقطع الأجل فيما بينكما يقول استحللتك بأجل آخر برضى منها ولا تحل لغيرك حتى تنقضي عدتها وعدتها حيضتان

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Al-Baqir and al-Sadiq interpret mutual agreement after the prescribed payment as her increasing the fee while he extends the term.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله عليهما السلام أنهما قالا هو أن يزيدها في الأجرة وتزيده في الأجل

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali says that without Umar intervention only the wretched would commit fornication.
rows.anchor: وكان علي يقول لولا ما سبقني به ابن الخطاب - يعني عمر - ما زنى إلا شقي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas condemns those who reject temporary marriage because the Prophet allowed it and did not prohibit it.
rows.anchor: وهؤلاء يكفرون بها ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أحلها ولم يحرمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai says reports on the preceding meanings are abundant or mass-transmitted from the Ahl al-Bayt Imams, and the cited reports are only samples.
rows.anchor: والروايات في المعاني السابقة مستفيضة أو متواترة عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام وإنما أوردنا طرفا منها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas describes temporary marriage among early Muslim travelers as a fixed-term arrangement in which a woman watched belongings and managed property; he says it was superseded by the chaste, non-fornicating rule.
rows.anchor: كان متعة النساء في أول الإسلام كان الرجل يقدم البلدة ليس معه من يصلح له ضيعته ولا يحفظ متاعه فيتزوج المرأة إلى قدر ما يرى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas asserts under oath that God revealed the verse with the words 'for a specified term,' although the standard recitation lacks them.
rows.anchor: فقلت ما نقرؤها كذلك فقال ابن عباس والله لأنزلها الله كذلك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reports that Ubayy ibn Ka'b's recitation included the words 'for a specified term.'
rows.anchor: عن قتادة قال في قراءة أبي بن كعب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says temporary marriage was an early-Islam travel arrangement until the verse limiting sex to spouses or owned women was revealed, after which every other sexual relation was forbidden.
rows.anchor: إنما كانت المتعة في أول الإسلام كان الرجل يقدم البلدة ليس له بها معرفة فيتزوج المرأة بقدر ما يرى أنه يقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai infers that this account makes the abrogation occur in Mecca, since the cited spouses-or-owned-women verse is Meccan.
rows.anchor: ولازم الخبر أنها نسخت بمكة لأن الآية مكية

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha answers that anyone seeking sexual relations beyond a wife or an owned woman has transgressed, citing 23:5–6.
rows.anchor: والذين هم لفروجهم حافظون إلا على أزواجهم أو ما ملكت أيمانهم فإنهم غير ملومين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the temporary-marriage verse was abrogated by divorce and waiting-period verses, including 65:1, 2:228, and 65:4.
rows.anchor: قال نسختها { يا أيها النبي إذا طلقتم النساء فطلقوهن لعدتهن والمطلقات يتربصن بأنفسهن ثلاثة قروء

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib says the inheritance verse abrogated temporary marriage.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب قال نسخت آية الميراث المتعة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud says temporary marriage was abrogated by the laws of divorce, dowry, waiting period, and inheritance.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال المتعة منسوخة نسخها الطلاق والصدقة والعدة والميراث

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali compares abrogation of temporary marriage by divorce, waiting period, and inheritance to Ramadan fasting replacing all fasts, zakat replacing charity, and sacrifice replacing other slaughter.
rows.anchor: عن علي قال نسخ رمضان كل صوم ونسخت الزكاة كل صدقة ونسخ المتعة الطلاق والعدة والميراث

rows.speaker: سبرة الجهني
rows.claim: Sabrata says the Prophet permitted temporary marriage at the conquest of Mecca; he and a cousin negotiated with a young woman, and the narrator had intercourse until the Prophet prohibited it.
rows.anchor: أذن لنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم عام فتح مكة في متعة النساء فخرجت أنا ورجل من قومي

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet prohibited temporary marriage and eating domestic donkey meat at Khaybar.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم نهى عن متعة النساء يوم خيبر وعن أكل لحوم الحمر الإنسية

rows.speaker: سلمة بن الأكوع
rows.claim: Salama ibn al-Akwa says the Prophet allowed temporary marriage for three days at the campaign of Awṭas and then prohibited it.
rows.anchor: عن سلمة بن الأكوع قال رخص لنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في متعة النساء عام أوطاس ثلاثة أيام ثم نهى عنها بعدها

rows.speaker: سبرة
rows.claim: Reports place the prohibition at the Farewell Pilgrimage, after leaving ihram there, or at the lesser pilgrimage of al-Qada; al-Tabatabai notes the dates conflict.
rows.anchor: سبرة روى أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم نهى عنها في حجة الوداع

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri reports that the Prophet permitted temporary marriage during the campaign of Tabuk.
rows.anchor: عن الزهري أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم جمع المتعة في غزوة تبوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because reports date the ban to many different occasions, al-Tabatabai suggests repeated prohibitions, yet says it is hard to believe close companions such as Ali, Jaber, and Ibn Mas'ud missed them.
rows.anchor: مع ملازمتهم للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وخبرتهم بالخطير واليسير من سيرته تأبى أن يخفى عليهم نواهيه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali says temporary marriage was initially allowed for those unable to marry, then abrogated when rules of marriage, divorce, waiting period, and inheritance were revealed.
rows.anchor: عن علي قال نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم عن المتعة وإنما كانت لمن لم يجد فلما نزل النكاح والطلاق والعدة والميراث بين الزوج والمرأة نسخت

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali rebukes Ibn Abbas as mistaken and says the Messenger of God prohibited temporary marriage.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب أنه قال لابن عباس إنك رجل تائه إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم نهى عن المتعة

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abu Dharr says temporary marriage was permitted to the Prophet's companions for three days and then prohibited.
rows.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال إنما أحلت لأصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم المتعة ثلاثة أيام ثم نهى عنه رسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas permits temporary marriage and agrees with his client that the allowance applied when women were scarce and circumstances were difficult.
rows.anchor: فرخص فيها فقال له مولى له إنما كان ذلك وفي النساء قلة والحال شديد فقال ابن عباس نعم

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar denounces men who contract temporary marriages despite the Prophet's prohibition and threatens to stone anyone he finds doing so.
rows.anchor: ما بال رجال ينكحون هذه المتعة وقد نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم عنها لا أوتى بأحد نكحها إلا رجمته

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Sabrata quotes the Prophet saying God has forbidden temporary marriage forever, ordering men to release their partners and not reclaim what they paid.
rows.anchor: إني كنت أذنت لكم في الاستمتاع ألا وإن الله حرمها إلى يوم القيامة فمن كان عنده منهن شي فليخل سبيلها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the Prophet's permission lasted only three days, with no allowance before or after.
rows.anchor: والله ما كانت المتعة إلا ثلاثة أيام أذن لهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فيها ما كانت قبل ذلك ولا بعد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets 'what you enjoy from them' as referring to temporary marriage.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد { فما استمتعتم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi describes a fixed-term contract with no ongoing claim after expiry, a required womb-clearing period for the woman, and no mutual inheritance.
rows.anchor: هذه المتعة الرجل ينكح المرأة بشرط إلى أجل مسمى فإذا انقضت المدة فليس له عليها سبيل وهي منه بريئة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud says the Prophet forbade castration when men campaigning without wives asked about it, and permitted marriage for a garment until a term; he recited 5:87.
rows.anchor: فنهانا عن ذلك ورخص لنا أن نتزوج المرأة بالثوب إلى أجل ثم قرأ عبد الله { يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تحرموا طيبات ما أحل الله لكم }

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar calls temporary marriage forbidden and asks why Ibn Abbas did not issue that permission during Umar's lifetime.
rows.anchor: عن نافع أن ابن عمر سئل عن المتعة فقال حرام فقيل له إن ابن عباس يفتي بها قال فهلا ترمرم بها في زمان عمر

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr confronts Ibn Abbas, saying travelers have spread his fatwa and poets are repeating it, then asks what they said.
rows.anchor: ذهب الركاب بفتياك وقالت فيه الشعراء قال وما قالوا قلت قالوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In response to a poem about his permission, Ibn Abbas denies giving that broad fatwa: he permitted temporary marriage only in necessity, like eating carrion, blood, or pork.
rows.anchor: لا والله ما بهذا أفتيت ولا هذا أردت ولا أحللت إلا للمضطر ولا أحللت منها إلا ما أحل الله من الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says temporary marriage is neither fornication nor ordinary marriage; its waiting period is one menstruation, and the partners do not inherit from one another.
rows.anchor: فقال لا سفاح ولا نكاح قلت فما هي؟ قال هي المتعة كما قال الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says temporary marriage was a divine mercy for Muhammad's community; the contract lasts a specified term for a specified fee, carries no inheritance, and may be renewed by mutual consent.
rows.anchor: ما كانت المتعة إلا رحمة من الله رحم بها أمة محمد ولولا نهيه عنها ما احتاج إلى الزنا إلا شقي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The same report says Ibn Abbas still regarded temporary marriage as lawful, despite Umar's prohibition.
rows.anchor: وأخبر أنه سمع ابن عباس أنه يراها الآن حلالا

rows.speaker: الحكم
rows.claim: Al-Hakam says the verse was not abrogated and cites Ali's statement that without Umar's ban only the wretched would commit fornication.
rows.anchor: وقال علي لولا أن عمر نهى عن المتعة ما زنى إلا شقي

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jaber says they practiced temporary marriage for handfuls of dates and flour during the Prophet's and Abu Bakr's time until Umar forbade it over Amr ibn Hurayth.
rows.anchor: كنا نستمتع بالقبضة من التمر والدقيق الأيام على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وأبي بكر حتى نهى عنه عمر

rows.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
rows.claim: Khawla tells Umar that Rabi'a ibn Umayya entered a temporary marriage with a woman who became pregnant; Umar says he would have stoned them had he prohibited it earlier.
rows.anchor: أن خولة بنت حكيم دخلت على عمر بن الخطاب فقالت إن ربيعة بن أمية استمتع بامرأة مولدة فحملت منه

rows.speaker: سليمان بن يسار
rows.claim: A Syrian visitor and a woman made a temporary contract before witnesses; when Umar questioned them, the man said the Prophet and the first two caliphs had allowed it, and Umar said he would have stoned him if he had forbidden it sooner.
rows.anchor: إن العزبة قد اشتدت علي فابغيني امرأة أتمتع معها قالت فدللته على امرأة فشارطها وأشهدوا على ذلك عدولا

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: In the same account, Umar says the distinction between marriage and fornication must be made publicly clear.
rows.anchor: بينوا حتى يعرف النكاح من السفاح

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jaber says temporary marriage continued under the Prophet, Abu Bakr, and Umar until late in Umar's caliphate.
rows.anchor: استمتعنا على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وأبي بكر وعمر وفي لفظ أحمد حتى إذا كان في آخر خلافة عمر

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar says temporary marriage is forbidden and that Umar would have stoned anyone who practiced it.
rows.anchor: أما إن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه لو أخذ فيها أحدا لرجمه بالحجارة

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: A report cited from Ibn al-Jawzi says Umar swore that he would stone a man who permitted temporary marriage.
rows.anchor: كان عمر رضي الله عنه يقول والله لا أوتى برجل أباح المتعة إلا رجمته

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Ibn Rushd's account from Jaber says the practice continued through half of Umar's caliphate, after which Umar prohibited it.
rows.anchor: تمتعنا على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وأبي بكر ونصفا من خلافة عمر ثم نهى عنها عمر الناس

rows.speaker: سلمة بن أمية بن خلف
rows.claim: Ibn al-Kalbi reports that Salama had a child with Salma after temporary marriage, denied the child, and that Umar then prohibited the practice.
rows.anchor: أن سلمة بن أمية بن خلف الجمحي استمتع من سلمى مولاة حكيم بن أمية بن الأوقص الأسلمي فولدت له فجحد ولدها فبلغ ذلك عمر فنهى المتعة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas rebukes Urwa for relying on Abu Bakr and Umar against reports from the Prophet, warning that continued rejection of the Prophet's teaching will bring punishment.
rows.anchor: والله ما أراكم منتهين حتى يعذبكم الله نحدثكم عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وتحدثونا عن أبي بكر وعمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai notes that Urwa's mother Asma had temporary marriage with al-Zubayr and gave birth to both Urwa and Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr.
rows.anchor: وأم عروة أسماء بنت أبي بكر تمتع منها الزبير بن العوام فولدت له عبد الله بن الزبير وعروة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
rows.claim: When Ibn al-Zubayr taunts Ibn Abbas for permitting temporary marriage, Ibn Abbas tells him to ask his mother; she says he was born from temporary marriage.
rows.anchor: فقالت ما ولدتك إلا في المتعة

rows.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر
rows.claim: Asma tells visitors that the Prophet permitted temporary marriage, in response to Ibn Abbas's direction to ask Ibn al-Zubayr's mother.
rows.anchor: فإذا امرأة ضخمة عمياء فقالت قد رخص رسول الله فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabatabai says the reported scene clearly concerns women's temporary marriage, as the surrounding reports also confirm.
rows.anchor: وشاهد الحال المحكي يشهد أن السؤال عنها كان في متعة النساء وتفسره الروايات الأخر أيضا
